one_liner: Slack has a broad Web API with OAuth, free developer sandboxes, incoming webhooks, and an official vendor-hosted MCP server at mcp.slack.com/mcp (admin approval may be needed).
auth_notes: The docs link a "Tokens and OAuth" section, and the MCP server uses OAuth. API_KEY (bot/user tokens, webhook URLs) is retained from standard Slack behaviour. The fetched pages only show the webhook URL as a static secret and do not show bot-token text, so confidence is medium.
access_notes: Anyone can join the free Slack Developer Program and provision a basic sandbox. Basic sandboxes have limits, including a one-month lifespan and no hosted functions. Some workflow features need a paid plan. Distributing apps to other workspaces goes through Marketplace review.
blocker_notes: No hard blocker. The MCP server goes through the standard Slack app approval process, so workspace admins may need to approve it. Marketplace distribution needs review.
